texts.title: Dry Tanks
texts.body: The admiral's report is one line long: the fleet has no helium-3. The ramscoops that fed it are someone else's, the exchange wants a broker's price, and every hull of {self.house} is riding at anchor with its guns cold while the lanes go on without it.

choices.buy_dear: Pay the broker's price. Eighteen credits for four tanks.
choices.strip_the_merchantmen: Requisition the merchantmen's fuel. Two tanks, and a harbour's grudge.
choices.ride_at_anchor: Let the fleet ride at anchor. Lanterns lit, guns cold.

texts.title: The Skimmer Barons
texts.body: A gas giant in a system of {self.house}'s has clouds worth skimming — helium-3, the fuel every navy in the Reach burns. A consortium has sent a factor with a draft contract and a case of wine; the house's own engineers have sent a plan and a bill. Whoever puts scoops in those clouds owns a thing the fleets cannot do without.

choices.raise_skimmers: Raise the house's own skimmers. Eight credits, four materials, the first six tanks.
choices.sell_the_concession: Sell the concession. Fourteen credits down, their ramscoops in our clouds.
choices.leave_it: Leave the clouds alone for now.

texts.title: A Vein of Rare Earths
texts.body: The claim-crews report that the belt {self.house} staked is richer than its ore: the rock carries rare earths, the stuff of drives and sensors, worth five of anything else that comes up. A refinery off-world will buy it raw; a chemist in the port will build the house a separator for ten credits and a share.

choices.refine_it: Build the separator. Ten credits; three crates of rare earths, and a trade.
choices.sell_raw: Sell the ore raw. Nine credits, and someone else's sensors.

texts.title: The Arms Broker
texts.body: A man with a false name and a real cargo manifest asks for an hour of {self.name}'s time. He has weapons-grade isotopes — two cases, enough to arm a battleship or a bastion — and he has heard that {self.house} is rich enough to want them and poor enough in deposits to have none. The Senate forbids the trade. The Senate is a long way away.

choices.buy_two: Buy both cases. Twenty-four credits, and a whisper in the Senate.
choices.report_him: Turn him over to the inspectors. The name that would not buy.

texts.title: The Fuel Contract
texts.body: {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} writes with the courtesy of someone whose fleet is nearly dry: would {self.house} sell four tanks of helium-3, at a fair price, between houses at peace? The house's tanks are full. Fuel is the one thing a navy cannot bluff.

choices.sell_four: Sell four tanks at a fair price. Sixteen credits and a kind word.
choices.sell_dear: Name a price that makes them wince. Twenty-four credits.
choices.refuse: Keep the fuel. Let them buy elsewhere.

texts.title: The Embargo
texts.body: {self.house} holds weapons-grade isotopes and is at war. The admiral wants them for the magazines. The chancellor wants an embargo declared, loudly, so the Senate sees who can afford to withhold them. A factor in a neutral port wants to sell them to anyone at all, quietly, for eighteen credits.

choices.arm_the_fleet: Break open the stores for the fleet. Two isotopes; the next broadside.
choices.embargo_them: Declare an embargo. Influence in the Senate.
choices.sell_to_both: Sell to both sides through the factor. Eighteen credits and a stain.
